title: Networking
summary: How containers talk to each other and to the outside world: network drivers, user-defined bridges and embedded DNS, how port publishing really works (NAT, docker-proxy, the Mac VM), and a debugging toolkit built on netshoot.
objectives: Describe what the bridge, host, none, overlay and macvlan drivers do and when to use each
Explain why user-defined bridges beat the default bridge (embedded DNS at 127.0.0.11, isolation)
Explain how `-p` works underneath: iptables/nftables DNAT, docker-proxy, and the extra hop through the VM on macOS
Connect containers to each other and to services on the host (`host.docker.internal`)
Use network aliases and multiple networks to model frontend/backend isolation
Debug connectivity and DNS with netshoot, curl, dig, ss and `docker network inspect`
